dimension_justifications.soundness: The scoped recorder-level interpretation is generally careful, and the manuscript distinguishes selection stability from null-calibrated detection. However, every central number is source-reported and cannot be recomputed from the frozen snapshot; the event streams and analysis code are absent, the active-recorder time index and allocation schedule are not specified at an executable level, and one discreteness argument conflicts with the paper's own half-integer medians. These are substantive verification gaps, not proof that the reported results are false.
dimension_justifications.presentation: The paper is anonymous, visually clean, within the nine-page main-text limit, and unusually candid about its composite intervention, post-treatment amendment, weak cells, and absent artifact bundle. The central reachability-versus-magnitude distinction is understandable. Presentation falls short of excellent because the reader must reconcile several overlapping selector, bootstrap, margin, rank-sum, and spectral readouts; the probe-arm candidate grid is not printed; and some table labels and definitions do not expose the claimed conjunction directly.
dimension_justifications.contribution: The two-layer reporting recommendation and the recorder-relative case study are useful and plausibly distinct. The contribution is nevertheless narrow: one private model checkpoint, one task, a composite partition-plus-allocation intervention, a reused development control, no arm-level false-positive calibration, and no verified artifact bundle. The supplied citation audit is partial, so the closest-work positioning cannot be fully verified here.

paper_summary: The paper studies positionwise identity-lock timing from an active-block recorder for a blockwise diffusion language model. It varies block length together with the required per-block step allocation at fixed model, questions, canvas, decoding rule, and total NFE, and reports that a registered min-max selector and a rank-sum comparison choose the configured length in five arms. It adds non-nested canvas-96 probes and exploratory spectral and content analyses, while explicitly limiting the conclusion to recorder-observable behavior and recommending separate reporting of a-priori boundary-set reachability and event-derived magnitudes.
strongest_verified_contribution: The strongest verifiable contribution in the frozen review object is the disciplined claim architecture: the manuscript consistently separates schedule-implied reachability, measured recorder-level selection, and unmeasured model or sampler mechanism, and it openly records the composite treatment and post-treatment scope amendment. The associated numerical five-arm result is clearly stated but cannot be independently verified from the included files.
strengths: The abstract, introduction, limitations, and conclusion consistently avoid a model-mechanism claim and distinguish selection stability from false-positive-controlled detection.
Figure 1 gives a clear qualitative picture of the active observation window, and Figure 2 separates the three main-arm profiles from the candidate-period summary.

The manuscript discloses the marginal L24 result, the single-locus L48 estimate, the weakest reused L32 control, the failed original permutation gate, and the post-treatment amendment rather than hiding them.
Anonymity appears intact; references start on page 9, so the main text is within the stated nine-page limit; reproducibility and AI-assisted preparation disclosures are present.
questions: Is the index s in Eq. (1) a global function-evaluation index, a block-local step, or the ordinal index among observations of a particular position, and how are unobserved times handled?
What exact block-index-to-step-count mapping is denoted by schedules such as [4]x8+[2]x8, and how does it sum to the fixed NFE for each arm?
Can the authors print the complete sep(P) vector for both L24 and L48 probes, rather than only P*, sep(32), and one mismatched P=48 cell?
How is the Table 2 probability of the registered conjunction computed when the row label displays only Pr[sep(L)>0] and the modal-period fraction is itself summarized over bootstrap replicates?

Will the event streams, executable scripts, exact question identifiers, and a releasable checkpoint specification be available to reviewers, given that the current package cannot rebuild any numeric result?

issues.location: Reproducibility statement on page 9; Appendix A.3 Table 9 on page 13; Appendix B, pages 17-18; included repository_inventory.md, experiment_registry.json, and method_provenance.tsv
issues.observed_evidence: The manuscript says the current package omits event streams, scripts, evidence ledgers, and the private checkpoint. The included inventory confirms that every named results JSON and analysis script is absent, and the registry marks the relevant runs reported_not_rerun. All central claim-map entries are source_reported/cannot_verify_locally.
issues.why_it_matters: The five-arm selector, bootstrap, rank-sum, permutation, and spectral numbers are the empirical basis of the paper. A provenance index containing unavailable paths and hash prefixes does not let a reviewer check extraction, recompute tables, or detect mismatched arm definitions.
issues.required_fix: Provide a reviewer-safe artifact containing the releasable event streams, exact question/decode identifiers, executable analysis and figure scripts, full configurations, environment lock, and cryptographic hashes; if the checkpoint cannot be released, provide a sufficiently precise checkpoint manifest and a runnable analysis-only path. Otherwise label every quantitative result as non-reproducible from the submission and narrow the empirical assurance accordingly.
issues.verification_test: From a clean environment, validate all file hashes, run the documented analysis-only command on the shipped events, and reproduce Tables 2-7 and 10-15 plus Figure 2 exactly or within declared tolerances.
issues.evidence_needed: The currently absent event records, code, configs, environment specification, complete hashes, logs, and reviewer-safe checkpoint provenance.

issues.location: Section 2, Eq. (1) and Table 1, pages 2-3; Appendix B determinism paragraph, page 18; Appendix C Tables 16-17, page 19
issues.observed_evidence: The recorder is said to expose only masked positions in the active block, but Eq. (1) defines lock time over recorded t >= s without defining whether s is global, block-local, or position-observation time or how missing observations are represented. Table 1 uses compact schedules such as [4]x8+[2]x8 without mapping counts to block indices or showing the NFE arithmetic. The included method provenance says the recorder and identity-lock definition are manuscript-specified only and event logs were not located.
issues.why_it_matters: The paper's central phenomenon is schedule-aligned position timing. Ambiguity in the time coordinate and in the composite allocation schedule prevents readers from reconstructing the estimand and deciding which periodicity is introduced mechanically by indexing or exposure.
issues.required_fix: Define the event schema and time axis formally, state the observation domain for each position, specify missing/terminal cases, and give an explicit block-by-block schedule for every arm with an NFE calculation and a small worked lock-time example.
issues.verification_test: Using the added schema and worked example, an independent reader should compute l_i,r, m(r), d(r), boundary sets, and sep(P) by hand; a schema validator should confirm every shipped event obeys those rules and every arm sums to the declared NFE.
issues.evidence_needed: Formal event-schema documentation, a toy trace, and the exact per-arm schedule configuration.

issues.location: Section 3.1, Tables 3-4, pages 5-6, especially the L24/L48 rows; claim that only the matching candidate has positive separation on page 4
issues.observed_evidence: Table 1 gives the probe candidate grid {8,16,24,32,48,64}, but Table 3 replaces all probe-arm candidate-separation cells with dashes and reports only P*. Table 4 adds sep(32) for both probes and one P=48 marginal cell for L24. Thus the manuscript does not display the complete values needed to inspect the argmax or the statement that only the selected period is positive; the referenced artifact is absent.
issues.why_it_matters: The non-nested probes are presented as the key check against fixed-32 structure, yet their selection result is less auditable on the page than the three main arms. This makes a headline claim depend on an unavailable artifact.
issues.required_fix: Print the full candidate-by-arm sep(P) vector for L24 and L48, identify all positive candidates, show the rank-sum candidate scores or ranks, and clearly distinguish point estimates from bootstrap summaries.
issues.verification_test: Recompute P* from the printed probe rows alone using the registered tie rule and confirm every prose statement about positivity, margins, and wrong candidates.
issues.evidence_needed: Complete probe-arm selector and rank-sum outputs for every registered candidate.

issues.location: Section 2, lines 159-161 on page 3; Tables 3 and 6 on pages 6-7
issues.observed_evidence: The text says integer lock times imply integer medians and an integer-valued min-max separation. With n=300, the usual median of integer observations can be half-integer, and the paper itself reports half-integer d(r) and separations, including 3.5 and 6.5.
issues.why_it_matters: This is an internal inconsistency in the explanation offered for a collapsed bootstrap band and the interpretation of zero misses. Discreteness may still matter, but the stated argument is false as written.
issues.required_fix: State the exact median convention and replace the integer-valued claim with a correct discreteness argument, then explain empirically why the L16 bootstrap collapses.
issues.verification_test: Enumerate the attainable median and sep values for n=300 under the implementation's median rule and confirm that every reported table value and the revised point-mass explanation are compatible.
issues.evidence_needed: Median implementation details and the bootstrap distribution or its unique-value counts.

issues.location: Section 2 registered criterion on page 3; Table 2 and caption on page 4; Section 3.2 on page 7
issues.observed_evidence: The registered criterion is defined as sep(P*)>0 plus a modal period fraction at least 0.95. Table 2 labels its first row only Pr[sep(L)>0] while the caption calls it the probability that the conjunction fires, and Section 3.2 calls the same 0.88-1.0 range the criterion-fire probability. The nesting of the mode-fraction calculation relative to the joint bootstrap is not shown.
issues.why_it_matters: A reader cannot tell whether the table reports one positivity event, a nested two-part criterion, or two summaries that coincide only because modal argmax equals one. This weakens claim legibility even if the values are correct.
issues.required_fix: Give pseudocode for the resampling hierarchy, label each statistic with its exact event, and report the two conjuncts in separate columns before their conjunction.
issues.verification_test: Map each Table 2 cell to a single pseudocode variable and independently derive the reported conjunction rate from the two printed components.
issues.evidence_needed: Resampling pseudocode and per-replicate indicator outputs.

issues.location: Section 5 and Appendix A.9 Tables 13-14, pages 8 and 16-17; included literature/citation_lock.json
issues.observed_evidence: The closest-work tables make detailed claims about what prior papers measure and omit, while the supplied citation lock is explicitly partial and records only one checked citation, for which support was not found for a removed sentence. No complete primary-source support audit is included.
issues.why_it_matters: The significance of a measurement canon depends on whether the claimed methodological gap is real. Under the frozen-snapshot protocol, that positioning is cannot_verify rather than established.
issues.required_fix: Add a complete primary-source citation-support ledger for every row-level comparison, with the exact local claim, supporting section/page, and an explicit cannot_verify marker where support is unavailable; soften novelty language not covered by verified sources.
issues.verification_test: For every factual cell in Tables 13-14 and every nearest-work sentence, a reviewer should be able to follow a ledger entry to a primary-source passage that entails the local claim without relying on absence inference.
issues.evidence_needed: A complete citation metadata and local-support audit for all cited closest works.

issues.location: Figure 2 and Tables 2-6 in the main text, pages 4-7; Appendix Tables 9 and 13-17, pages 13 and 16-19
issues.observed_evidence: The paper is visually clean, but Figure 2's profile traces, edge markers, and labels are small at print size, and the argument is distributed across many dense tables with repeated caveats and provenance references. Page 6 is mostly blank while several later tables are compressed.
issues.why_it_matters: The reader must repeatedly cross-reference definitions, caveats, and appendix tables to reconstruct which result supports which scoped claim. This increases verification cost for an already multi-layer argument.
issues.required_fix: Use the available page space to enlarge Figure 2, consolidate the headline five-arm estimates into one self-contained table, and add a compact claim-to-readout panel distinguishing descriptive selection, stability, calibration, and exploratory checks.
issues.verification_test: At normal print scale, all Figure 2 labels and edge encodings should be legible, and each headline claim should be checkable from one figure/table plus one definition without an appendix lookup.
issues.evidence_needed: Revised camera-ready layout and a print-size visual inspection.

ethics_concerns: No direct human-subject, privacy, safety, or deployment ethics issue is evident in the frozen snapshot. The private checkpoint and missing artifact bundle are reproducibility and provenance concerns rather than an ethics flag.
llm_usage_disclosure: This review was produced by an isolated AI subagent for internal pre-submission quality control. The manuscript itself includes an AI-assisted preparation disclosure on page 18 stating that Figure 1 was image-generated and that an AI assistant edited prose and LaTeX; Figure 1 is explicitly labeled qualitative and non-evidentiary.
evidence_that_would_raise_score: A self-contained reviewer artifact that exactly reproduces all headline tables and Figure 2 from shipped events and scripts.
A formal, executable definition of the active-recorder time index and every per-block allocation schedule, supported by toy traces and schema validation.
Complete probe-arm candidate vectors and clearly separated selector, stability, margin-calibration, and rank-sum readouts.
A fresh, independently collected L32/NFE48 control and a factorial partition-by-allocation or dual-recorder comparison that narrows the causal ambiguity.
A complete primary-source citation-support audit demonstrating that the two-layer reporting recommendation fills a real closest-work gap.
evidence_that_would_lower_score: Any recomputation that changes the selected period, bootstrap conjunction rate, rank-sum argmax, or corrected-margin conclusions.
Evidence that lock-time indexing or missing-observation handling mechanically guarantees the reported boundary pattern beyond the scoped schedule geometry already disclosed.
Complete probe vectors showing unreported positive wrong candidates or sensitivity of P* to the tie rule or candidate grid.
Primary-source checks showing that the claimed closest-work gap or row-level comparisons are unsupported.
Failure of the descriptive period-following result on a fresh control drawn independently of estimator development.
review_limitations: The central event streams, scripts, result files, and private checkpoint were not included, so all headline numeric claims remain cannot_verify rather than falsified.
Outside literature was intentionally not consulted under the blind-snapshot protocol; novelty and citation judgments are limited to the partial citation lock and manuscript text.
The PDF's complete text and all 19 rendered pages were inspected, but no source TeX or build log was included for an independent compile check.
